Done. Reflection complete.

What this near-miss exposed (6.15% vs gold 6.16%): the data extraction was trivial — two 26-week bill discount rates (2.33% and 2.35%) — but the answer hinged entirely on computing the realized-volatility estimator with full precision. My error was truncating sqrt(52) to 7.2 instead of 7.2111, which flipped the hundredths digit. This is a genuine, recurring class (quant estimators on Bulletin rates), not per-question trivia.

Saved:
- New reference `references/statistical-estimators-volatility.md` with the full recipe: vol% = sqrt(periods)·|ln(r2/r1)|·100, weekly⇒×52, LOG return (not simple/difference), realized variance = squared return with no mean-subtraction or N−1, and the worked example + the three distinct failure modes (truncated constant→6.15, simple return→6.19, 365/7 factor→6.17, pre-rounded return→6.13).
- A pointer line in SKILL.md's reference list so a future agent loads it when a question asks for log returns / realized volatility / annualized vol.

Memory was already full (2,132/2,200), so I routed this to the skill references where it fits better and has room — it's the same "carry full precision, round once" family already documented there for currency/geomean questions.
